description.narrative:
The commitment of Vietnam to net zero at COP26 has opened opportunities for RE transition in Vietnam. However, it also brings many challenges in implementation, especially on land use change, traditional livelihood loss, inequality and policy gaps in agriculture,environment, resilient livelihoods, construction and transportation.
Together with its benefits, RE development, which has just started in recent years, also causes unexpected consequences such as high land acquisition, livelihood change, elated solar power development, causing social conflicts and high end-of-life wastes, etc. The research provides recommendations for a better road map of energy transition in the following areas • The power development plan should be integrated simultaneously with other national master plans of socio-economy, environmental protection, agricultural production, forest protection and development etc. • The investment for renewable energy development encourages the diversified investment forms from private sectors and foreign funds in both power sources and transmission lines. • Legal policies on solar power development, especially rooftop solar power, should be completed in order to ensure the stable energy supplying, rights of investors, lower land-use change; and minimize socio-environment consequences. •Better social responsibilities of project developers in creating new jobs for local residents, especially affected people, women and ethnic minorities, social welfare policies, vocational training in collaboration with local authorities. • Promoting residential roles in public consultation and information disclosure; monitoring project activities and their environmental protection. In addition, the country needs to build a long-term and transparent policy roadmap towards protecting the interests of investors, especially local users who have installed solar power facilities at their houses and farms.
Influencing and promoting energy transition toward becoming more equal, inclusive and sustainable is one of the top priorities of the Oxfam Climate Resilience program in Vietnam. In its new country strategy (2020-2025), the country programme aims to influence the current growth-based development model to shift to a Human Economy Development Model, which puts people and the planet before profit.
